key_insight: Motion 3-to-4 is a feed-forward framework that reconstructs high-quality 4D (time-varying 3D) objects from a single monocular video (and an optional 3D reference mesh) by explicitly separating static shape from dynamic motion, enabling accurate geometry and motion recovery despite limited data and monocular ambiguity.
problem_solved: Recovers both detailed 3D geometry and temporally coherent motion from a single-view video input — a task made difficult by limited 4D training data and inherent depth/motion ambiguity in monocular capture.
method: Decompose 4D synthesis into static 3D shape reconstruction and dynamic motion estimation so each subtask is easier to solve robustly in a feed-forward pass.
Optionally condition on a provided 3D reference mesh to anchor geometry; otherwise infer a high-quality static shape from the video.
Use temporal consistency and motion-aware neural representations to produce coherent 4D outputs (time-indexed meshes or neural fields) suitable for rendering and animation.
impact: Enables practitioners to generate temporally coherent 3D animations from simple monocular videos, lowering the barrier for 4D content creation in AR/VR, VFX, and robotics without large multi-view datasets.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input monocular video (+ optional mesh) → static 3D shape branch → motion estimation branch → fused 4D output
Before/after comparison: original video frames vs. reconstructed time-varying 3D meshes or rendered animations
Flow visualization: per-frame motion vectors or deformation fields overlaid on the static geometry to show temporal coherence
Ablation chart: qualitative/quantitative comparison showing benefits of decomposition and optional reference mesh
paper_authors: Hongyuan Chen, Xingyu Chen, Youjia Zhang, Zexiang Xu, Anpei Chen
